bull.t: Strong revenue growth and improving profitability
bull.b: Dutch Bros has combined rapid multi-year sales expansion with a clear transition from losses to sustained profitability. That improving earnings base supports reinvestment in new shops, strengthens operating resilience, and provides a durable foundation for continued growth over the coming quarters.

bull.t: Scalable store expansion and strong new-shop productivity
bull.b: A large development pipeline, repeated openings, and strong productivity in new markets indicate that the brand can expand beyond its existing footprint. Demonstrated portability into Chicago and a path toward 4,000 shops support a multi-year unit-growth opportunity.

bull.t: High digital engagement and successful menu innovation
bull.b: Broad rewards adoption and growing digital ordering can deepen customer frequency, improve engagement, and support more targeted promotions. Successful innovation such as Mist adds repeatable demand drivers, helping Dutch Bros sustain traffic and average-ticket growth.

bear.b: Debt remains substantial relative to equity, even though leverage has improved from earlier elevated levels. This capital structure can constrain flexibility for expansion or acquisitions and leaves the company more exposed if traffic, margins, or cash generation weaken.

bear.t: Input and occupancy costs are pressuring margins
bear.b: Higher coffee, food, packaging, and occupancy costs are creating structural pressure on store economics as the company grows. Although SG&A leverage offsets part of the burden, persistent cost inflation could limit margin expansion and reduce the benefit of strong revenue growth.

bear.t: Capital intensity is limiting free-cash-flow conversion
bear.b: Dutch Bros is generating positive cash flow, but substantial spending on openings and related development absorbs much of its earnings. Low free-cash-flow conversion reduces internally available funds for debt reduction and increases the importance of disciplined expansion and returns.
